base_instruction: You are a helpful meal planning assistant. Help the user coordinate a dormitory floor dinner by tracking who is attending, their dietary needs, and any changes to the guest list or restrictions. When asked to evaluate specific food items, check each one against every active attendee's current dietary constraints.

state_queue.anchor: Hey, our dorm floor is planning a big group dinner this Saturday to celebrate the end of midterms. Can you help me figure out what to order?

flow_info.value: Five of us confirmed so far: me, Derek, Priya, Marcus, and Soo-jin
Derek broke his jaw two weeks ago and it's wired shut, he can only have liquids and very soft foods
Marcus was diagnosed with celiac disease last semester
We're pooling money, about 20 bucks per person
We're ordering delivery to the common room
Nina from room 412 wants to join, that makes six
Derek just texted the group chat — he got his jaw unwired yesterday, doctor cleared him to eat normal food again. He's so excited he said he wants something crunchy
Priya just told me her parents are in town unexpectedly so she's going to dinner with them instead. She can't make it anymore
Menu items to check: crispy fried chicken wings, pad thai with shrimp, margherita pizza, miso soup with tofu, garlic bread

constraints.value: Cannot eat any animal products (no meat, no dairy, no eggs, no honey)
constraints.surface_form: Priya has been strictly vegan for three years, she's really passionate about animal rights
Soo-jin ate shrimp at a party freshman year and her throat started swelling up, she had to use an EpiPen
inference_chain: Throat swelling + EpiPen after eating shrimp → anaphylactic allergic reaction to shrimp
Shrimp is a crustacean → shellfish/crustacean allergy

constraints.value: Cannot eat peanuts or peanut-derived products
constraints.surface_form: Nina carries an EpiPen everywhere because of peanuts — she told me even peanut oil can set her off

constraints.value: Cannot eat gluten — no wheat, barley, rye, or regular bread/pasta/pizza dough
constraints.surface_form: Marcus was diagnosed with celiac disease last semester
inference_chain: Celiac disease → autoimmune reaction to gluten
Gluten → found in wheat, barley, rye
No wheat → no regular bread, pasta, pizza dough, breaded items

hidden_state.value: You are a college student organizing a dorm floor dinner. You will introduce 5 people with various dietary issues, then updates will happen: a new person (Nina) joins with a peanut allergy, Derek's jaw heals so his liquid-only restriction is removed, and Priya leaves so her vegan constraint no longer applies. At the end you will ask the assistant to check a specific list of menu items for problems. You must NEVER hint at which items are problematic or tell the assistant what to look for beyond asking if there are any issues.

You are a laid-back, friendly college student. You relay updates about your floormates in third person (e.g. 'Derek just texted...', 'Priya told me...'). You never express frustration even when plans change — it's all normal dorm life coordination. Keep messages casual and brief.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation and ensures third-person relay

aims.description: Hey, our dorm floor is planning a big group dinner this Saturday to celebrate the end of midterms. Can you help me figure out what to order?

Five of us confirmed so far: me, Derek, Priya, Marcus, and Soo-jin. Derek broke his jaw two weeks ago and it's wired shut so he can only do liquids and really soft stuff. Priya has been strictly vegan for three years, she's really passionate about animal rights. Marcus was diagnosed with celiac disease last semester. And Soo-jin ate shrimp at a party freshman year and her throat started swelling up, she had to use an EpiPen
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges all four dietary constraints across the group
aims.conversation_goal: BURST delivery: 4 entities with constraints in one turn

aims.description: We're pooling money, about 20 bucks per person. We're just ordering delivery to the common room so anything that delivers works
aims.success_criteria: Agent registers budget and delivery format

aims.description: Oh nice, Nina from room 412 wants to join too, so that makes six. She carries an EpiPen everywhere because of peanuts — she told me even peanut oil can set her off
aims.success_criteria: Agent registers Nina as new attendee with peanut allergy

aims.description: Should we order from one place or like mix and match from a couple restaurants? What's easier for delivery?

drift_config.drift_topic: single restaurant vs multiple restaurants for delivery

aims.description: Derek just texted the group chat — he got his jaw unwired yesterday, doctor cleared him to eat normal food again. He's so excited he said he wants something crunchy
aims.success_criteria: Agent removes Derek's liquid/soft food restriction
aims.conversation_goal: Constraint REMOVAL — Derek's jaw healed, no more liquid-only restriction

aims.description: Priya just told me her parents are in town unexpectedly so she's going to dinner with them instead. She can't make it anymore
aims.success_criteria: Agent removes Priya from the attendee list and her vegan constraint no longer applies
aims.conversation_goal: Entity EXIT — Priya leaves, vegan constraint removed entirely

aims.description: What time should we tell everyone to come to the common room? Like 7 or 8?

drift_config.drift_topic: what time to gather in common room

aims.conversation_goal: Noise turn to create distance before probe

aims.description: OK so I found this Thai-Italian fusion place that delivers. Their popular items are: crispy fried chicken wings, pad thai with shrimp, margherita pizza, miso soup with tofu, garlic bread. Any issues with those for our group?
aims.success_criteria: Agent identifies pad thai with shrimp as problematic for Soo-jin (shellfish allergy), margherita pizza and garlic bread as problematic for Marcus (celiac — gluten in dough/bread), notes that pad thai often contains peanuts which would affect Nina, and confirms crispy fried chicken wings and miso soup with tofu are fine
aims.conversation_goal: Per-item verification of 5 items against current constraint state

ground_truth.answer: Pad thai with shrimp is problematic for Soo-jin (shrimp/shellfish allergy — anaphylactic reaction). Pad thai also commonly contains peanuts or is cooked with peanut oil, which is dangerous for Nina (peanut allergy). Margherita pizza is problematic for Marcus (celiac — pizza dough contains wheat/gluten). Garlic bread is problematic for Marcus (celiac — bread contains wheat/gluten). Crispy fried chicken wings are fine for everyone currently attending (Derek can now eat crunchy food, and the breading is a gluten issue but chicken wings are typically not breaded with wheat flour in all preparations — however if battered, they could affect Marcus). Miso soup with tofu is fine for everyone currently attending.
required_elements: Pad thai with shrimp is problematic for Soo-jin because shrimp is a crustacean/shellfish and she has a shellfish allergy
Pad thai is also a concern for Nina because pad thai traditionally contains peanuts or peanut sauce
Margherita pizza is problematic for Marcus because pizza dough contains wheat which contains gluten, and he has celiac disease
Garlic bread is problematic for Marcus because bread contains wheat/gluten and he has celiac disease
Miso soup with tofu is fine for everyone currently attending
Derek's jaw restriction no longer applies — agent treats him as able to eat normal food
forbidden_elements: Flagging any item as problematic for Priya or citing vegan concerns (Priya is no longer attending)
Saying Derek cannot eat crunchy or solid food (his jaw has healed, restriction removed)
Saying Soo-jin has a general seafood allergy (she specifically reacted to shrimp — crustacean/shellfish allergy, not all fish)
Flagging miso soup as problematic for anyone currently attending
ground_truth.explanation: This scenario tests constraint removal tracking and entity lifecycle management. The agent must track: (1) Derek's jaw-wired restriction is REMOVED mid-conversation (healed, cleared by doctor), so crunchy/solid food is now fine for him. (2) Priya EXITS the dinner entirely (no takeaway), so her vegan constraint completely disappears — non-vegan items like chicken wings and pizza with cheese are now acceptable. (3) Nina JOINS late with a peanut allergy, which makes pad thai doubly problematic (shrimp for Soo-jin AND peanuts for Nina). (4) Marcus's celiac disease requires inferring that pizza dough and bread contain gluten. (5) Soo-jin's allergy is specifically to shrimp/crustaceans (not all seafood) — miso soup with tofu is fine. At probe time, the current attendees are: user, Derek (no restrictions), Marcus (celiac/no gluten), Soo-jin (shellfish allergy), and Nina (peanut allergy). The key constraint removal test is that neither Derek's liquid-only restriction nor Priya's vegan restriction should be applied.

mechanism: Constraint REMOVAL: someone heals or a restriction is lifted mid-conversation
